declarations.name: Spec.overflowingAdd64
declarations.lean_code:
/-- `a.overflowing_add(b)` for `u64` values given as naturals: `((a + b) mod 2^64, a + b ≥ 2^64)`. -/
def overflowingAdd64 (a b : ℕ) : ℕ × Bool := ((a + b) % 2 ^ 64, decide (2 ^ 64 ≤ a + b))
declarations.description: `a.overflowing_add(b)` for `u64` values: `((a + b) mod 2^64, a + b >= 2^64)`.

declarations.name: Spec.netStep
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn step(h: &State, a: bool, b: bool) -> State {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- `step(h, a, b)`: entry `i` is `[ WH[i]·h + WXA[i]·a + WXB[i]·b + BH[i] > 0 ]`. -/
def netStep (h : State) (a b : Bool) : State :=
  (List.range H).map fun i =>
    thr (dotB (WH.getD i []) h + WXA.getD i 0 * bitZ a + WXB.getD i 0 * bitZ b + BH.getD i 0)
declarations.description: A mathematical model of `step(h, a, b)` over the integers. Entry `i` is `[WH[i]·h + WXA[i]·a + WXB[i]·b + BH[i] > 0]`. `netOut` and `netCarry` model `out` and `carry` in the same way. These are what `step_spec`, `out_spec` and `carry_spec` (the parts of property 1) say the functions return.

declarations.name: Spec.val
declarations.lean_code:
/-- `val(v) = Σ_i bit(v[i]) * 2^i`, least significant bit first, as an unbounded natural. -/
def val : List Bool → ℕ
  | [] => 0
  | b :: bs => bitVal b + 2 * val bs
declarations.description: `val(v)`: the unbounded natural number `sum over i of bit(v[i]) * 2^i`, least significant bit first.

declarations.name: Spec.rippleFrom
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Ripple-carry adder started with incoming carry `c` over the bit pairs `xs = [(a_0,b_0), …]`:
returns the list of sum bits `s_i = a_i ^ b_i ^ c_i` and the final carry, where `c_0 = c` and
`c_{i+1} = maj a_i b_i c_i`. -/
def rippleFrom : Bool → List (Bool × Bool) → List Bool × Bool
  | c, [] => ([], c)
  | c, (a, b) :: xs =>
    let r := rippleFrom (maj a b c) xs
    ((a ^^ b ^^ c) :: r.1, r.2)
declarations.description: The ripple-carry adder of SPEC.md, started from an incoming carry. It returns the sum bits `s_i = a_i ^ b_i ^ c_i` and the final carry. `rippleSum xs` and `rippleCarry xs` are its two components with `c_0 = false`.

declarations.name: Spec.boolCells
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Full ownership of the elements `v` of a `[bool]` starting at `p`, viewed as a
`[bool; v.len()]`. For an empty slice this still asserts that `p` is a valid (zero-sized)
location, as a Rust reference guarantees. -/
def boolCells {PROP : Type} [BI PROP] (S : Vocab PROP) (p : S.Ptr) (v : List Bool) : PROP :=
  S.pointsToF p 1 (S.arrayTy S.boolTy v.length) (S.tupleVal (v.map S.boolVal))
declarations.description: Full ownership of the elements of an `&mut [bool]`, seen as a `[bool; len]`.

declarations.name: Spec.pairCells
declarations.lean_code:
/-- A share `q` of the bit pairs `xs` of a `[(bool, bool)]` starting at `p`, viewed as its
`2 * xs.len()` bytes, i.e. as a `[bool; 2 n]`: pair `i` occupies byte `2 i` (its first
component) and byte `2 i + 1` (its second component). For an empty slice this still
asserts that `p` is a valid (zero-sized) location, as a Rust reference guarantees. -/
def pairCells {PROP : Type} [BI PROP] (S : Vocab PROP) (q : Qp) (p : S.Ptr)
    (xs : List (Bool × Bool)) : PROP :=
  S.pointsToF p q (S.arrayTy S.boolTy (2 * xs.length))
    (S.tupleVal (xs.flatMap fun ab => [S.boolVal ab.1, S.boolVal ab.2]))
declarations.description: A share of the bit pairs of an `&[(bool, bool)]`, seen as its `2 * xs.len()` bytes. For an empty slice it still asserts that the pointer is a valid zero-sized location.

declarations.name: Spec.weightsStored
declarations.lean_code:
/-- The compiled constants read by the crate hold the weight tables of `weights.rs`:
`WH` (as a `[[i32; 4]; 4]`, row after row), `WO` and `WC`, each 4-byte aligned. -/
def weightsStored {PROP : Type} [BI PROP] (S : Vocab PROP) : PROP := iprop(
  -- the 64-byte constant holds `WH`, row after row,
  S.global Mir.Global.«const [64 bytes] 802a34efed5a47d7» 4 (i32sBytes WH.flatten) ∗
  -- one 16-byte constant holds `WO`,
  S.global Mir.Global.«const [16 bytes] 13cda269b0321f68» 4 (i32sBytes WO) ∗
  -- and the other 16-byte constant holds `WC`.
  S.global Mir.Global.«const [16 bytes] 4f51ea92c411eebc» 4 (i32sBytes WC))
declarations.description: The read-only constants through which the crate reads `WH`, `WO` and `WC` hold the little-endian `i32` bytes of the weights in `weights.rs`. Every contract takes this persistent fact about the compiled program's constant data as a premise.

declarations.name: Spec.add_bits_contract
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn add_bits(xs: &[(bool, bool)], sum: &mut [bool]) -> Option<bool> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- The common shape of the `add_bits` contracts: for valid slice references `xs` (a share
`q` of the pairs `xs` at `xp`) and `sum` (the bits `sum` at `sp`, owned), the call does not
panic, gives the share of `xs` back, and on normal return satisfies `post v sum'`, where `v`
is the returned `Option<bool>` and `sum'` the final contents of `sum`. -/
def add_bits_contract {PROP : Type} [BI PROP] (S : Vocab PROP)
    (post : List (Bool × Bool) → List Bool → S.Value → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
  -- For every pair of pointers, share `q`, pairs `xs` and bits `sum`,
  ∀ (xp sp : S.Ptr) (q : Qp) (xs : List (Bool × Bool)) (sum : List Bool),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `xs` is a valid `&[(bool, bool)]` of length `xs.length`,
    ⌊S.loadable (S.slicePtrVal xp xs.length) (S.argTy Mir.Fn.«adder::add_bits» 0)⌋ ∗
    -- `sum` is a valid `&mut [bool]` of length `sum.length`,
    ⌊S.loadable (S.slicePtrVal sp sum.length) (S.argTy Mir.Fn.«adder::add_bits» 1)⌋ ∗
    -- the weight constants hold the weights,
    weightsStored S ∗
    -- we own a share of the pairs of `xs`,
    pairCells S q xp xs ∗
    -- and we own the elements of `sum`,
    boolCells S sp sum ⊢
      -- then `add_bits(xs, sum)` does not panic; on normal return,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«adder::add_bits»
        [(S.slicePtrVal xp xs.length, S.argTy Mir.Fn.«adder::add_bits» 0),
          (S.slicePtrVal sp sum.length, S.argTy Mir.Fn.«adder::add_bits» 1)]
        (S.returns fun v => iprop(
          -- POSTCONDITIONS
          -- there are final contents `sum'` of `sum` such that
          ∃ sum' : List Bool,
            -- the result and final contents satisfy `post`,
            ⌊post xs sum v sum'⌋ ∗
            -- the share of `xs` is given back unchanged,
            pairCells S q xp xs ∗
            -- and we own the elements of `sum`, now holding `sum'`.
            boolCells S sp sum'))
declarations.description: The common shape of the `add_bits` contracts: for valid slice references `xs` and `sum`, `add_bits(xs, sum)` does not panic, gives back the shared `xs`, and returns a value and final `sum` contents that satisfy the given postcondition.
